text:
support-sandra: Heads up — we started getting a wave of latency complaints from a handful of hosted customers ~03:10 UTC. P95 is up ~1.4x but p99 is around 3x (baseline ~220ms, now ~700ms). They all hit model xlarge (seq=1024) on gpu-prod-3 pool. No obvious error codes, just long tail responses and some streaming stalls.

support-sandra: dashboard link: https://dash.redwood.example/p99-spike (screenshots in thread). Several support tickets opened, customers reporting timeouts on token streams. Repro steps attached. cc @oncall-bot @eli (eng-infra)

deploy-bot: Canary rollout complete: CUDA runtime rollout "cuda-12.3-canary" to pool gpu-prod-3 at 02:45:12 UTC. Hosts affected: gpu-prod-3-[12,13,14,15]. Rollout ID: r-2026-11-03-02045

eli (eng-infra): Thanks @support-sandra. This timing lines up with the CUDA rollout. Can you paste a couple of request IDs and example trace ids? Also confirm if logs show any nvme errors or kernel warnings (dmesg).

support-sandra: RequestIDs: rq_8b3f2a, rq_8b3f2b, rq_8b3f2c. I pulled the pod logs for rq_8b3f2a and see repeated stalls: "kv_cache_miss; waiting for disk read" and occasionally "io_wait > 500ms" in our runtime logs. No explicit OOMs.

jules (storage-ops): Can you run blktrace / iostat on one of the affected hosts? I'm curious if there's NVMe tail latency or scheduling backlog. If you don't have access, I can pull from monitoring.

alex (eng-runtime): Noted. Our runtime does aggressive continuous batching; if storage I/O for the kv cache is delayed it propagates as tail latency. Two quick asks: 1) try disabling prefix caching for a test route to see if p99 drops, 2) collect `perf top` or `perf record -a` during a spike. Also paste the output of `nvidia-smi` and `nvme top` from affected hosts.

mira (eng-sre): P95 vs P99 suggests a small subset of requests are hitting an IO path. Could be driver/kernel interaction (async IO submission throttling) after the CUDA/drivers update. We should triage with a repro: run a synthetic workload that mimics our streaming generation + concurrent background IO (fio) to the NVMe. Steps below.

quan (eng-ml): Quick note — model xlarge uses larger KV cache and more frequent NVMe lookups for cold seq=1024. If driver introduced higher NVMe submission tail, that matches the symptoms.

eli (eng-infra): I'm running a quick check. From gpu-prod-3-13: `dmesg | tail -n 50` shows a handful of `nvme nvme0: abort status: 5` and a few `nvme_core: asynchronous abort` entries starting at 02:48 UTC. Also seeing `blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector ...` — copying exact lines into thread.

support-sandra: Copy of runtime snippet for rq_8b3f2a:
```
[2026-11-03T03:11:22Z] request rq_8b3f2a: start streaming
[2026-11-03T03:11:22Z] kv_cache lookup miss for shard 12 -> read nvme0n1p1 offset 0x9f000
[2026-11-03T03:11:23Z] nvme read latency 612ms
[2026-11-03T03:11:23Z] stream stall detected, dropping to fallback chunking
```

jules (storage-ops): That's consistent with NVMe tail. I'll queue `fio --name=nvme_tail_test --filename=/dev/nvme0n1 --rw=randread --bs=4k --iodepth=32 --numjobs=4 --runtime=120` on one host and compare latency distribution. If latencies spike above ~200ms frequently it's the device/driver.

mira (eng-sre): Meanwhile let's limit customer impact: mitigation options — 1) pin traffic off gpu-prod-3 pool (route config change), 2) roll back the CUDA/driver update on the affected hosts, 3) temporarily increase our request timeout/retries/enable more aggressive local caching. Which is fastest?

eli (eng-infra): Fastest immediate: shift traffic off the pool with a route override (we can redirect to gpu-prod-1/2 with minimal churn). I'll prepare a routing override and coordinate with Support. Rolling back drivers is slower (coord ops), but we can target 2-3 hosts as an experiment.

alex (eng-runtime): For an immediate test, I can flip a per-route feature flag to disable prefix/KV caching for a small percentage of traffic (1-5%) to see if p99 improves for those requests. If it does, confirms NVMe path is hot.

support-sandra: Doing route override to reduce customer impact now. Will update once done.

oncall-bot: Paging oncall: incident tagged P2 - potential customer-impacting latency. Assigned to @mira (eng-sre).

mira (eng-sre): Thanks. @eli please proceed with traffic shift. @alex toggle the cache flag to 2% canary. @jules run fio and paste histo.

jules (storage-ops): FIO run results (gpu-prod-3-13):
```
fio: randread iodepth=32 bs=4k numjobs=4 runtime=120
lat (usec):  max=734000, 95th=210000, 99th=580000, avg=24000
```
That's pretty bad — 99th ~580ms consistent with runtime traces.

alex (eng-runtime): Cache flag at 2% is live. Early look: the canary requests show p99 ~230ms (closer to baseline) vs 700ms on normal. That strongly implicates the NVMe path.

mira (eng-sre): Great signal. Proceed with traffic shift now. Eli, can you update the routing policy and also annotate nodes so we don't auto-scale into that pool?

eli (eng-infra): Routing override applied — rerouted traffic for affected customers to gpu-prod-1/2. Also cordoned gpu-prod-3-[12..15] to avoid further scheduling. K8s commands used:
```
kubectl label nodes gpu-prod-3-13 node.kubernetes.io/cordoned=quarantine
kubectl patch svc redwood-api -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"route-override":"gpu-prod-1"}}}}}'
```

support-sandra: Early telemetry after shift: p99 for those customers down to ~260ms within ~3m. They're still cautious but acknowledging improvements.

eli (eng-infra): I'll start a targeted rollback of CUDA on gpu-prod-3-13 and gpu-prod-3-14 to the previous driver (nv 535.86 -> 532.02). Will attach playbook.

quan (eng-ml): If rollback fixes tail, we should block the rest of the rollout and open a kernel/driver review with vendor. Also add a perf test to our release gate exercising cold kv cache paths.

eli (eng-infra): Rollback completed on 13 and 14. After reboot and sanity checks, fio on 13 now shows:
```
fio histo: max=120000 usec, 95th=45ms, 99th=90ms, avg=6ms
```
Runtime traces for requests hitting 13 show p99 back near baseline.

mira (eng-sre): Excellent. Action items:
- Stop cuda-12.3 rollout and mark canary paused (eli)
- Reimage/rollback remaining hosts in pool only after triage (eli + storage-ops)
- Add fio + synthetic generator to our CI gating for driver/kernel updates (alex + quan)
- Add an alert for nvme blktrace errors and `nvme_core` aborts (jules + mira)
- Postmortem if rollback exceeds 4 hours or customers report reoccurrence (mira)

eli (eng-infra): Stopped the rollout and flagged rollout ID r-2026-11-03-02045 as paused. I'll schedule deeper NVMe vendor debug and open a vendor ticket with logs.

support-sandra: Customer notifications sent — we're monitoring. I'll keep this thread updated with ticket numbers. Thanks all. :thumbsup: 

mira (eng-sre): Closing loop — for immediate mitigation we used routing override + targeted rollback. Root cause suspected: interaction between CUDA 12.3 userland driver + kernel NVMe submission path causing occasional aborts and long tail. Triage ongoing with vendor.

support-sandra: Final update: customers on the impacted pool report latency normalized. We'll keep pool cordoned until infra confirms vendor patch or we patch our gating. Last seen baseline restored at 04:02 UTC.

oncall-bot: Incident P2 resolved to P3 (monitoring) by @mira. If new regressions appear reopen the incident.
